findings.title: SEMP custody is not encoded in the crosswalk
findings.finding: The four cited SEMP files are absent from the reviewed C2 commit and production-base tree. They exist only as untracked files in the preserved original checkout, where their bytes match the cited hashes. The crosswalk gives relative repository paths and says its source clauses are checked in; it does not state local-only custody, the original workspace revision, or the missing-from-base condition. The companion evidence discloses untracked generated views at line 85 but does not cover the canonical model and schema. The same checked-in-custody overstatement also applies to the two plan/execution paths at lines 18-26, which are likewise original-checkout-only.

source_proof.production_base_docs_semp: git ls-tree -r --name-only 45210704b8de2d7b1360b6d32657cd17791bdd77 docs/semp returned no paths
source_proof.manifest_proof: Original SEMP model lines 3-18 carry MODEL-USHSO-SEMP-001, version 0.5.1, candidate/proposed/not_approved/not_requested states; generated manifest lines 1-16 bind the model, schema, generator, and hashes.
source_proof.companion_evidence: verification/research-program/pr-001/crosswalk-evidence.json:38-45 hashes SEMP files through absolute original-checkout paths; :83-87 says generated views remain untracked but does not state canonical-model/schema custody.

findings.action: Add explicit source_root, source_workspace_head, retained workspace-manifest SHA, present_in_base=false, and local_only custody/disposition for every external SEMP and plan source; qualify the checked-in-source wording and generated_semp_views_changed field so they cannot be read as production-base provenance.

findings.title: SEMP gate, transition, and decision-work-package IDs have no destination or retained constraint
findings.finding: The planning-baseline and program/subject entries at lines 154-166 each carry a disposition and destination_prs. The 12 GATE IDs, 13 GTR IDs, and 11 DWP IDs at lines 168-170 are bare arrays with neither per-ID destinations nor an explicit retained constraint. The package_disposition at line 172 clearly scopes the release_packages array at line 171, and the disposition at line 178 scopes source/evidence/conflict IDs; neither supplies a disposition for gates, transitions, or decision work packages. The verification statement at line 486 checks production_boundaries only.

source_proof.original_semp_model: The cited IDs are present in the original-only SEMP model under review_gates.gates (12), review_transitions (13), and decision_and_evidence_readiness.work_packages (11).
source_proof.structural_check: All 16 work-package rows, all 13 production-boundary rows, and all 8 ADR rows have non-empty destination/constraint or disposition fields; only the three SEMP ID arrays lack that treatment.

findings.action: Add group-level or per-ID destination_prs plus retained constraints/dispositions for GATE, GTR, and DWP entries, or explicitly document an inherited destination/constraint rule that covers each array.
